title: The Warrens: Paranormal Power Couple
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck profile Ed and Lorraine Warren, Connecticut paranormal investigators who founded the New England Society for Psychic Research in 1952 and became famous through publicity, books, lectures, and their museum. They walk through their best-known cases: the Perron family haunting in Rhode Island (basis for the first Conjuring film), the Annabelle doll in Hartford, the Amityville Horror, the Enfield poltergeist in London (basis for The Conjuring 2), the Arnie Johnson demonic-possession murder case in Brookfield, and the Snedeker haunting in Southington (The Haunting in Connecticut). They discuss the hoax allegations (Ray Gorton's claim that the Snedeker book was fiction, the Lutz and Ronald DeFeo lawyer's claim the Amityville story was made up over wine, the 1997 New England Skeptical Society review), the Warrens' financial profits, the Conjuring film franchise's grosses, and the 2017 allegations by Judith Penny, along with the restrictive consulting contract Lorraine had with New Line Cinema. The episode closes with listener mail correcting a pronunciation point and a sign-off.

entities.name: New England Society for Psychic Research

segments.title: Opening banter and the Conjuring debate
segments.summary: Hosts greet listeners, chat about New Year's hopes, Kpop Demon Hunters, and whether they've seen The Conjuring, and introduce the Warrens as paranormal power couple who made money from scams.

segments.title: Warrens' origins and the Conjuring franchise earnings
segments.summary: Background on the New England Society for Psychic Research founded in 1952, the Warrens' childhoods in Bridgeport, their marriage, and how they got into ghost hunting. The Conjuring films have grossed at least $2.3 billion.
topics: New England Society for Psychic Research

segments.title: Warrens' fees and the Perron farmhouse haunting
segments.summary: The Warrens did not charge families for help but earned money through lectures, books and a museum. The Perron family haunting in Rhode Island, the basis for the first Conjuring film, is introduced.

segments.title: Perron haunting details and the witch ghost
segments.summary: The Perron family's haunting at the Harrisville farmhouse, the seance in which Carolyn is thrown across the room, and the Warrens' attribution to a dead witch. The haunting reportedly stopped when the family left after ten years.

segments.title: Annabelle doll in Hartford
segments.summary: A Raggedy Ann-style doll given to a nurse named Donna is said to be possessed by a demon posing as the ghost of Annabel Higgins. The Warrens took the doll into their museum under glass.

segments.title: Amityville Horror and the Lutz family
segments.summary: The 1974 DeFeo family murders at 112 Ocean Avenue in Amityville, the Lutz family's brief stay, the claimed paranormal events, the Warrens' investigation, and the Ghost Boy photo.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break before the next case.

segments.title: Enfield poltergeist in London
segments.summary: The 1977 Enfield case with the Hodgson family, Janet's possession by a ghost named Bill Wilkins, and the Society for Psychical Research's investigation. Linked to The Conjuring 2.

segments.title: Warrens and the Enfield case, Poltergeist book deal
segments.summary: Hosts describe more Enfield phenomena and the Warrens' 1978 claim of a poltergeist, followed by a sale of the story to New Line Cinema. Mention of the SPR audio tapes and a documentary.

segments.title: Arnie Johnson demonic possession murder case
segments.summary: In 1981 in Brookfield, Connecticut, Arnie Johnson stabbed his landlord and claimed a demon in him committed the crime after he dared it to possess him during an exorcism of David Glatzel. He was convicted of manslaughter. The Warrens are tied to the case.

segments.title: Snedeker haunting in Southington
segments.summary: The Snedeker family moved into a former Hallahan funeral home in Southington, Connecticut. Son Philip's room had been a casket display room. Mother Carmen described abuse by a ghost; the Warrens appeared on Sally Jesse Raphael.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break before the critical analysis section.

segments.title: Evidence, skeptics, and the 1997 review
segments.summary: The Warrens' hard evidence and artifacts, the 1997 New England Skeptical Society review that found the evidence unfalsifiable, and Lorraine's response. Discussion of harms from exploiting families and the satanic panic.

segments.title: Hoax claims: Snedeker book, Amityville, Enfield
segments.summary: Ray Gorton's 2009 claim that the Snedeker book was fiction, the Amityville hoax claim by DeFeo's lawyer William Weber over wine, the Lutz response, and questions about the Enfield investigation. Also mentions a blog about the Arnold estate.

segments.title: Judith Penny allegations and Lorraine's contract
segments.summary: Judith Penny's 2017 claims of a relationship with Ed Warren from age fifteen, Lorraine's alleged pressure for an abortion, and the consulting contract that barred depicting the Warrens in criminal or sexual conduct. The Warrens' museum closed in 2019, and the Society continues under son-in-law Tony Spera.

segments.title: Listener mail on pronunciation
segments.summary: A listener writes in to say Chuck was right about the pronunciation of 'villa' as Spanish rather than Italian.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts give the email address and close the episode.
